runs.content:
**Investigation idea:** Three separate podcast-recommender picks now point at behavioral economics/marketing psychology, and Learning's own Seth Godin page — literally about marketing psychology — has never absorbed any of them. podcasts/suggestions.md has suggested Choiceology (2026-07-02), Behavioral Grooves (2026-07-16), and now Nudge (today's 2026-08-06 batch) across five weeks, each independently framed as filling a behavioral-economics gap. Nudge's own "Why for Fred" text goes further than the previous two, naming the target directly: it's "the direct Seth Godin/marketing-psychology lane in Fred's profile that neither prior behavioral-economics suggestion actually addresses head-on." learning/person-seth-godin.md — the wiki's dedicated page on exactly this territory (Core Themes rows on "Attention and trust" and "Remarkability," a Books table including *This is Marketing*) — has no Podcasts section and references none of the three shows; none have been picked up into podcasts/podcast-list.md as adopted listening either. Next step: pick one (Nudge is the closest match per the recommender's own framing, and its 20–30 min format is the lowest commitment) and cross-link it from person-seth-godin.md once tried — the same "recommender keeps finding the same unaddressed gap" pattern already flagged for Sports Betting on 2026-07-09.

**Cross-domain connection:** Today's Training Data recommendation names a concrete real-world data point — ElevenLabs' ~$400M revenue on ~400 people — for the exact "who captures the productivity gains" question AI & Tech's own future-of-work page poses only in the abstract. podcasts/suggestions.md's newest batch (week of 2026-08-06) recommends Training Data citing "ElevenLabs' Mati Staniszewski (building a $400M-revenue audio AI business at ~400 people)" as a headline data point. ai-tech/ai-future-of-work.md's own "Distributional Effects" section asks, unresolved: "If AI makes a lawyer 3x more productive, does the lawyer earn 3x more, does the firm charge 3x less, or does the firm keep the margin?" — and its only concrete real-world evidence so far is Clapham's "16% youth employment decline among 22–25s" cross-link, a job-loss data point. ElevenLabs, at roughly $1M+ revenue per employee, is the positively-framed mirror image of the same question: a named, dated example of AI-leveraged lean-team economics concentrating outsized revenue in a tiny headcount. Next step: once the episode is heard, add ElevenLabs as a named case study to ai-future-of-work.md's Distributional Effects section, cross-linked from the podcast suggestion.

**Cross-domain connection:** Today's FoundMyFitness recommendation names two specific new dementia-prevention mechanisms — sauna use and glucosamine — that Health's own primary source page doesn't cover at all, a sharper instance of the still-open Dementia Matters connection from a week ago. podcasts/suggestions.md's newest batch recommends FoundMyFitness specifically for "a July 2026 episode on glucosamine and Alzheimer's, and research showing sauna use 4–7×/week correlates with 65–66% lower dementia risk." health/source-wood-brain-sharp-2026.md — the wiki's existing primary dementia-prevention source — runs 7 numbered intervention categories plus the 14 Lancet risk factors, but neither sauna use nor glucosamine appears anywhere in it. This sharpens rather than repeats the 2026-07-30 connection (Dementia Matters, logged in general "dedicated clinical-research show" terms) — here the recommendation names two specific, citable findings the existing page is missing outright. Next step: if Fred picks up FoundMyFitness, add sauna-frequency and glucosamine as new items to source-wood-brain-sharp-2026.md's Interventions list.

Thursday focus (Books + Podcasts): deep-read podcasts/suggestions.md (today's new week-of-2026-08-06 batch: Training Data, Forward Guidance, FoundMyFitness, Nudge), podcasts/podcast-list.md, books/suggestions.md, books/reading-list.md. Books had no new activity since the 2026-08-03 Gates of Rome correction (book-recommender's next scheduled run is 2026-08-15), so all three findings came from today's fresh podcast-recommender batch read against existing wiki pages. No items resolved this run — checked finance/ideas/ for a GAW.L page (still absent) and games/prototypes.md's table (still the placeholder row), both still open from prior runs.

**Cross-domain connection:** Learning's own decision-making framework is literally built on poker theory, and Sports Betting — a domain about making betting decisions — has never cited it. learning/framework-decision-making.md ("Making Good Decisions," AltMBA P3) is explicitly sourced from Annie Duke's *Thinking in Bets* and states its core insight as "life is poker, not chess... you can make the perfect decision and lose the hand," with "a good decision is one where you judged the odds well — even if you lost" as the headline maxim, plus a dedicated Sunk Cost Trap section. This is not a loose analogy to Sports Betting's mission — it's the same discipline stated in more general form. sports-betting/overview.md frames its whole approach as "systematic, model-informed betting with disciplined bankroll management" (explicitly not recreational gambling), and sports-betting/bankroll-management.md's own Key Concepts section names Closing Line Value (CLV) as "the primary long-run metric" specifically because it measures decision quality independent of any single bet's outcome — the exact decisions-vs-outcomes distinction Duke's framework formalises. bankroll-management.md already cross-links two Finance sizing pages (concept-kelly-criterion.md, burry-vs-kelly-sizing.md) but nothing from Learning, and framework-decision-making.md's own Cross-References list three other Learning pages and nothing outside the domain at all. Next step: add a line to sports-betting/bankroll-management.md citing framework-decision-making.md's process-over-outcome framing as the conceptual foundation under CLV as a metric, and add a reverse link back from framework-decision-making.md.

Wednesday focus (Health + Learning): deep-read health/overview.md, health/my-protocol.md, both Health source pages (Wood, Godin), learning/overview.md, learning/courses.md, framework-decision-making.md, and the two Kevin Kelly source pages. log.md showed zero new activity in either domain since the 2026-08-04 thinker run (no new clippings, no scheduled-task output touching Health or Learning), and the two longstanding open ideas in this area (Health's empty Goals section waiting on the AltMBA opportunity-cost exercise; Outlive/Number Go Up both still unread on the reading list) remain unresolved with no change to report. Today's finding came from reading courses.md's "Books Referenced in AltMBA" table against Sports Betting's own domain pages rather than from any new source material — no items resolved this run.
